newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore replaces HK as Asia's least bureaucratic.
newsitem.headline: Singapore replaces HK as Asia's least bureaucratic.

text.p: Singapore has been judged the least bureaucratic centre in Asia in a recent survey, replacing Hong Kong in the run-up to its return to China on July 1.
The Asian Intelligence report by the Hong Kong-based Political and Economic Risk Consultancy said Hong Kong slipped into second place as it risks rising bureaucracy after the transition.
It said rules in Hong Kong could be changed to reflect those of Beijing and added that efficiency could be eroded if experienced, skilled workers started to leave the territory.

"As we warned a year ago, the exodus from the civil service in the run-up to the July 1 transition could be stretching the supply of experienced manpower in the civil service, resulting in greater inefficiency, the report, seen by Reuters on Sunday, said.
"In particular, British citizens are going to experience more red tape, considering the relatively large number of UK nationals in such professions as law and journalism", it said.

The survey was conducted by asking expatriate businessmen in Asia to grade countries on how bureaucratic red tape detracted from the business environment. The consulting firm said it received an average of 40 responses per country.

It said while Singapore's promotion to top spot shows that Singapore's "strong interventionist government is not necessarily the same thing as a bureaucratic government", civil servants can sometimes be "overly officious and demand that things be done exactly by the book."
Outside Hong Kong and Singapore, PERC noted in the survey that the Philippines bureacracy has improved "considerably" in the 1990s while that of South Korea was voted bottom of the list.

In South Korea, it said "important decisions are left to the discretion of individual bureacrats" and "the government's generally capricious enforcement makes the overall business environment unpredictable."
